answer: An atlas marketplace gives a fixed credit budget each round to an audited kernel of sponsors. A beacon marks the reset. Sponsors can split credits among agents, but every transfer debits the sender; endorsement chains cannot mint credits. Votes consume credits, with no account bonus. A thousand aliases behind one sponsor thus share its original budget. More influence requires persuading or corrupting other independent sponsors, not generating keys. This assumes honest sponsor admission and global accounting that prevents double spending; captured sponsors may still sell their budgets.
